symbols.name: B_n
symbols.role: Monte Carlo size for the retained empirical bootstrap

symbols.name: m_K
symbols.role: fixed distance from the identified set to the boundary of \(K\)

symbols.name: C_delta
symbols.role: contact-local radius dominating the Gaussian local-index bound

symbols.name: T_bar
symbols.role: radius of the compact interior LAN experiment

symbols.name: theta_minus
symbols.role: raw Watson endpoint before intersection with \(K\)

symbols.name: theta_plus
symbols.role: raw Watson endpoint before intersection with \(K\)

symbols.name: Theta_hat_tot
symbols.role: every-sample endpoint estimator distinct from the population \(K\)-restricted sublevel set

symbols.name: I_star
symbols.def: Conditional on \(W_1,\ldots,W_n\), \(I_{bj}^{*}\), \(1\leq b\leq B_n\), \(1\leq j\leq n\), are mutually independent with \(P(I_{bj}^{*}=i\mid W_1,\ldots,W_n)=1/n\)

symbols.name: W_star
symbols.def: \(W_{bj}^{*}=W_{I_{bj}^{*}}\) for \(1\leq b\leq B_n\) and \(1\leq j\leq n\)

symbols.name: delta_hat_star
symbols.def: \(\widehat\delta_{n,b}^{*}\) is obtained by applying the same centered covariance, ridge map \(R_n\), and plug-in definitions used for \(\widehat\delta_n\) to \(W_{b1}^{*},\ldots,W_{bn}^{*}\)

symbols.name: Theta_hat_star_tot
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Theta_{n,b}^{*,\mathrm{tot}}\) is obtained by applying the construction of \(\widehat\Theta_n^{\mathrm{tot}}\), including the common ridge and positive-part conventions, to \(W_{b1}^{*},\ldots,W_{bn}^{*}\)

symbols.name: L_ret
symbols.def: Let \(E_{n,b}^{*}=(\inf\widehat\Theta_{n,b}^{*,\mathrm{tot}},\sup\widehat\Theta_{n,b}^{*,\mathrm{tot}})\) and \(E_n=(\inf\widehat\Theta_n^{\mathrm{tot}},\sup\widehat\Theta_n^{\mathrm{tot}})\). Set \(\widehat{\mathbb L}_n^{\mathrm{ret}}=M_n^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}J_{n,b}\operatorname{Dirac}_{E_{n,b}^{*}}\) if \(M_n>0\), and set \(\widehat{\mathbb L}_n^{\mathrm{ret}}=\operatorname{Dirac}_{E_n}\) if \(M_n=0\)
symbols.role: measurable retained-law output with zero-retention fallback

symbols.name: Q_ret
symbols.def: For the lower and upper coordinate marginals \(\widehat{\mathbb L}_{n,s}^{\mathrm{ret}}\), define \(Q_{n,s}^{\mathrm{ret}}(u)=\inf\{x:\widehat{\mathbb L}_{n,s}^{\mathrm{ret}}(( -\infty,x])\geq u\}\)

symbols.name: Dq
symbols.type: Fr\'{e}chet derivative of the quadratic score
symbols.def: the derivative obtained by differentiating \(q_P(\theta)\) through \(\Sigma_{zz}^{-1}\Sigma_{zy}\) and \(\Sigma_{zz}^{-1}\Sigma_{zx}\)

symbols.name: Dq_reg
symbols.type: Fr\'{e}chet derivative of the ridge-totalized score
symbols.def: the derivative of \(S\mapsto\mathfrak q_n(S;\theta)\), including the derivative of \(R_n(S_{zz})\)

symbols.name: xi_i
symbols.space: independent \(N(0,1)\) variables independent of the sample

symbols.name: C_n
symbols.space: closed subsets of \(K\), including the empty set

symbols.name: D_n
symbols.space: data-measurable random closed subsets of \(K\), including \(\varnothing\)
symbols.role: decision class for minimax lower bounds

symbols.name: d_arrow
symbols.sig: \(d_{\to}:\mathcal K_0(K)\times\mathcal K_0(K)\to[0,\infty]\), where \(\mathcal K_0(K)\) contains all closed subsets of \(K\), including \(\varnothing\)
symbols.def: \(d_{\to}(A,B)=0\) if \(A=\varnothing\); \(d_{\to}(A,B)=+\infty\) if \(A\neq\varnothing\) and \(B=\varnothing\); and \(d_{\to}(A,B)=\sup_{a\in A}\inf_{b\in B}|a-b|\) otherwise

symbols.name: a_nh
symbols.def: \(a_{n,h}=\sqrt{1-h/\sqrt n}\) for \(h\in[0,\bar H]\) and sufficiently large \(n\)

symbols.name: P_nh
symbols.def: under \(P_{n,h}\), \(Z_1,Z_2,\epsilon_x,\epsilon_y\) are independent \(N(0,1)\), \(X=Z_1+\epsilon_x\), and \(Y=a_{n,h}Z_2+\epsilon_y\); equivalently, \(W_i\sim N(0,\Sigma(a_{n,h}))\) with \(\theta_0=0\) and \(\gamma=(0,a_{n,h})^{\prime}\)

symbols.name: P_int_nt
symbols.def: under \(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}\), \(Z_1,Z_2,\epsilon_x,\epsilon_y\) are independent \(N(0,1)\), \(X=Z_1+\epsilon_x\), and \(Y=(a_{\mathrm{int}}+t/\sqrt n)Z_2+\epsilon_y\) for \(t\in[-\bar T,\bar T]\); equivalently, \(W_i\sim N(0,\Sigma(a_{\mathrm{int}}+t/\sqrt n))\) with \(\theta_0=0\) and \(\gamma=(0,a_{\mathrm{int}}+t/\sqrt n)^{\prime}\)

assumptions.condition: The observations \(W_1,\ldots,W_n\) are independent draws from \(P\) and satisfy \(E_P[W_i]=0\).

standard.name: strong-instrument relevance bounded away from zero

assumptions.condition: The score variance satisfies \(c_{\sigma}\leq\inf_{\theta\in K}\sigma_P(\theta)\leq\sup_{\theta\in K}\sigma_P(\theta)\leq C_{\sigma}\).
The sharp set satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(\Theta_I(P),\partial K)\geq m_K\).
A contact-local law at index \(n\) satisfies \(0\leq\delta(P)\leq C_{\delta}n^{-1/2}\).

standard.name: strict interiority of the inequality constraint

assumptions.condition: A competing sequence \(D_n\) satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{h\in[0,\bar H]}P_{n,h}\{\Theta_I(P_{n,h})\subseteq D_n\}\geq1-\eta\).
A competing sequence \(D_n\) satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{t\in[-\bar T,\bar T]}P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}\{\Theta_I(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}})\subseteq D_n\}\geq1-\eta\).

definitions.name: published \(p=2\) sharp score and endpoint identity
definitions.construction: Watson et al. (2024, Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7) establish, for the scalar \(L_2\) leakage model with \(p=2\), the sharp identity \(\Theta_I(P)=\{\theta\in K:q_P(\theta)\leq0\}\). If \(\delta(P)<0\), this set is empty. If \(\delta(P)\geq0\), the raw analytic endpoints are defined and the identity becomes \(\Theta_I(P)=K\cap[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]\). This identity is a published input, not a contribution of the project.

definitions.name: measurable covariance ridge convention
definitions.construction: For the original sample, every empirical-bootstrap resample, and every multiplier derivative, replace an inverse of an empirical instrument covariance block \(S_{zz}\) by \(R_n(S_{zz})=(S_{zz}+n^{-2}I_d)^{-1}\). Compute reduced forms and \(\mathfrak q_n\) from this same map on every sample; no procedure is conditioned on empirical invertibility.

definitions.name: totalized positive-part endpoint construction
definitions.construction: Estimate the observable covariance, apply the common ridge map \(R_n\) to compute \(\widehat\alpha_n\), \(\widehat\beta_n\), and \(\widehat\delta_n\), and report \(\widehat\Theta_n^{\mathrm{tot}}\); a negative empirical slack is mapped to the singleton \(\{\widehat{\check\theta}_n\}\). The construction is defined even when \(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n}\) is singular.

definitions.name: retained empirical bootstrap
definitions.construction: Choose a deterministic sequence \(B_n\to\infty\). Conditional on the original sample, generate exactly \(B_n\) mutually independent Efron \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) candidate samples using \(I_{bj}^{*}\), center each resample by its own mean, and compute \(\widehat\delta_{n,b}^{*}\) and \(\widehat\Theta_{n,b}^{*,\mathrm{tot}}\) with the same ridge map \(R_n\). Retain candidate \(b\) exactly when \(J_{n,b}=\mathbf 1\{\widehat\delta_{n,b}^{*}>0\}=1\). If \(M_n>0\), output the empirical endpoint-pair law \(\widehat{\mathbb L}_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\) over the retained draws and its left-continuous coordinate quantiles \(Q_{n,-}^{\mathrm{ret}}\) and \(Q_{n,+}^{\mathrm{ret}}\). If \(M_n=0\), output the Dirac law at the original totalized endpoint pair. This is a finite Monte Carlo realization of Watson et al.'s Theorem 4 feasibility filter and the \(p=2\) \(\texttt{leakyIV}\) branch; it is measurable on every original sample and every candidate resample.

definitions.name: one-dimensional multiplier score hull
definitions.construction: Evaluate the ridge-totalized score \(\mathfrak q_n\) and its derivative on every sample, use Gaussian multipliers to calibrate the one-sided supremum over \(K\), and invert the same studentized inequality for every \(\theta\in K\) to obtain \(C_n\). The output may be empty, but it is always a closed subset of \(K\).

definitions.name: contact--interior coupling handle
definitions.construction: Exploit that the score process is a studentized quadratic polynomial in the single index \(\theta\), couple its finite coefficient vector before taking the supremum, and transfer the root-\(n\) score error through the deterministic quadratic growth modulus of \(q_P\).

definitions.name: positive-definite contact witness
definitions.construction: Specialize to \(d=2\), \(\tau=1\), and \(K=[-2,2]\). For each \(h\in[0,\bar H]\), use \(P_{n,h}\) with covariance \(\Sigma(a_{n,h})\). The compatibility regime is \(C_{\delta}\geq\bar H\), \(c_{\beta}\leq1\), \(m_{\Sigma}\leq(3-\sqrt5)/2\), \(M_{\Sigma}\geq(3+\sqrt5)/2\), \(M_8\geq1920\{(3+\sqrt5)/2\}^4\), \(c_{\sigma}\leq\sqrt2\), \(C_{\sigma}\geq10\), and \(m_K\leq1\).

definitions.name: positive-definite fixed-interior witness
definitions.construction: Specialize to \(d=2\), \(\tau=1\), and \(K=[-2,2]\). Fix \(a_{\mathrm{int}}\in(0,1)\) with \(1-a_{\mathrm{int}}^2>\delta_0\), and use \(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}\) for \(t\in[-\bar T,\bar T]\). The compatibility regime is \(c_{\beta}\leq1\), \(m_{\Sigma}\leq(3-\sqrt5)/2\), \(M_{\Sigma}\geq(3+\sqrt5)/2\), \(M_8\geq1920\{(3+\sqrt5)/2\}^4\), \(c_{\sigma}\leq a_{\mathrm{int}}\), \(C_{\sigma}\geq10\), and \(m_K\leq1\).

definitions.name: contact-honest confidence-set class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak D_{\eta}^{\mathrm{ct}}=\{(D_n)_{n\geq1}:D_n\text{ is a data-measurable closed subset of }K\text{ and satisfies }\mathrm{ass:contact\mbox{-}competitor\mbox{-}coverage}\}\)

definitions.name: interior-honest confidence-set class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak D_{\eta}^{\mathrm{int}}(a_{\mathrm{int}},\bar T)=\{(D_n)_{n\geq1}:D_n\text{ is a data-measurable closed subset of }K\text{ and satisfies }\mathrm{ass:interior\mbox{-}competitor\mbox{-}coverage}\}\)

statements.statement: For every law \(P\) for which the reduced-form primitives are defined, the sharp identified set is the always-defined sublevel set \(\Theta_I(P)=\{\theta\in K:q_P(\theta)\leq0\}\). If \(\delta(P)<0\), then \(\Theta_I(P)=\varnothing\). If \(\delta(P)\geq0\), the raw analytic endpoints \(\theta_-(P)\) and \(\theta_+(P)\) are real-valued and \(\Theta_I(P)=K\cap[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P_W\), the structural equations and \(L_2\) leakage restriction give \(\alpha(P)-\theta_0\beta(P)=\gamma\) and hence \(\theta_0\in\Theta_I(P)\). Therefore the parameter-margin condition forces \(\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)\in\operatorname{int}(K)\), so \(\Theta_I(P)=[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]\), for every \(P\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{ct}}(C_{\delta})\cup\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)\); no \(K\)-truncation occurs on either maintained regime.
statements.justification: The lemma gives the raw square-root formulas their exact domain and shows that the maintained margin condition removes parameter-space truncation wherever endpoint asymptotics are used.
statements.gap: Watson et al. give the quadratic reduction, but the contact analysis requires an explicit distinction between the globally defined sublevel set and partial raw endpoints.
statements.consumer: All endpoint limits and lower-bound paths can invoke raw endpoints without evaluating a square root at negative slack or silently dropping the intersection with \(K\).

statements.statement: Under the compatibility regime in the Gaussian-witness definition and whenever \(\sqrt n\geq2\bar H\), uniformly over \(h\in[0,\bar H]\), \[(3-\sqrt5)/2\leq\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma(a_{n,h}))\leq\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma(a_{n,h}))\leq(3+\sqrt5)/2,\] \(E_{P_{n,h}}[\|W_i\|_2^8]\leq1920\{(3+\sqrt5)/2\}^4\), and \(\sigma_{P_{n,h}}(\theta)^2=4(\theta^2+a_{n,h}^2)(1+\theta^2)\in[2,100]\) for every \(\theta\in[-2,2]\). Moreover, \(\beta=(1,0)^{\prime}\), \(\alpha=(0,a_{n,h})^{\prime}\), \(\theta_0=\check\theta=0\), \(\gamma=(0,a_{n,h})^{\prime}\), and \(\delta(P_{n,h})=h/\sqrt n\leq C_{\delta}/\sqrt n\). The raw endpoints are therefore defined and \(\Theta_I(P_{n,h})=[-\sqrt{h/\sqrt n},\sqrt{h/\sqrt n}]\subset(-2,2)\), so \(\operatorname{dist}(\Theta_I(P_{n,h}),\partial K)=2-\sqrt{h/\sqrt n}\geq2-1/\sqrt2>1\); no \(K\)-truncation occurs. Hence \(P_{n,h}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{ct}}(C_{\delta})\) along the full path. The experiment \(\{P_{n,h}:h\in[0,\bar H]\}\) is locally asymptotically normal and mutually contiguous on compact \(h\)-sets.
statements.justification: The explicit numerical bounds certify that the entire local path satisfies positive definiteness, fixed relevance, score nondegeneracy, moment control, and parameter-space interiority.
statements.gap: Watson et al.'s simulations stay away from equality and do not provide a LAN path through their feasibility boundary.
statements.consumer: The path supplies both the exact early kill test and the local-minimax converse experiment.

statements.statement: Let \(B_n\to\infty\) and use exactly the Efron candidate-resampling, strict-feasibility retention, empirical-law output, and zero-retention fallback in the retained-bootstrap definition. Uniformly for \(h\in[0,\bar H]\) under \(P_{n,h}\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\delta_n-h/\sqrt n)\Rightarrow Z\) with \(Z\sim N(0,4)\), and the ordered endpoints of \(\widehat\Theta_n^{\mathrm{tot}}\) satisfy \(n^{1/4}(\widehat\theta_-^{\mathrm{tot}},\widehat\theta_+^{\mathrm{tot}})\Rightarrow(-\sqrt{(h+Z)_+},\sqrt{(h+Z)_+})\). Conditional on the contact-limit realization, the candidate-retention probability converges to \(\Phi\{(h+Z)/2\}\), whose infimum over \(h\in[0,\bar H]\) is \(\Phi(Z/2)>0\) almost surely. Thus \(B_n\to\infty\) makes the fallback negligible: \(\sup_{h\in[0,\bar H]}P_{n,h}(M_n=0)\to0\). Writing \(\widehat{\mathbb L}_{n,+}^{\mathrm{ret}}\) for the upper-coordinate marginal, the bounded-Lipschitz distance between its pushforward under \(u\mapsto n^{1/4}u\) and \(\mathcal K_h(Z)\) converges to zero in probability uniformly in \(h\); the lower-coordinate marginal converges to the reflected kernel. Centering the retained upper-coordinate law at \(n^{1/4}\widehat\theta_+^{\mathrm{tot}}\) subtracts \(\sqrt{(h+Z)_+}\) from the random kernel.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies the fourth-root sampling law and the data-dependent selection kernel of a fully specified finite-sample retained-resampling algorithm, including its asymptotically negligible fallback.
statements.gap: It strictly qualifies Watson et al.'s Theorem 4: their differentiability argument omits the square root at \(\delta=0\) and their feasibility filter conditions on a nondegenerate random event.
statements.consumer: Users of \(\texttt{leakyIV}\) obtain the correct contact-local reference law and a diagnostic for retained-resample distortion.

statements.statement: There exist constants \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\pi>0\) and a nonempty compact interval \(H_0\subseteq[0,\bar H]\) such that, uniformly for \(h\in H_0\), with probability at least \(\pi+o(1)\) the bounded-Lipschitz distance between the conditional ordinary Efron-bootstrap law of the centered, \(n^{1/4}\)-scaled endpoint pair and its sampling law exceeds \(\varepsilon\). For the exact \(B_n\)-candidate retained algorithm in the retained-bootstrap definition, the same conclusion holds for \(\widehat{\mathbb L}_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\) because its scaled coordinate marginals converge to the random kernel \(\mathcal K_h(Z)\) and its reflection, while \(\sup_{h\in H_0}P_{n,h}(M_n=0)\to0\). Consequently, percentile intervals formed from the ordinary conditional law or from the left-continuous retained quantiles \(Q_{n,-}^{\mathrm{ret}}\) and \(Q_{n,+}^{\mathrm{ret}}\) fail to attain uniform endpoint coverage; the finite Monte Carlo realization of the feasibility-retained workflow in Watson et al.'s Theorem 4 is not contact-uniform.
statements.justification: A random limiting kernel turns a qualitative boundary warning into a falsifiable nonuniformity theorem for a named implementation.
statements.gap: Andrews treats a projected boundary estimator and Fang--Santos treat directionally differentiable maps; neither covers the half-Hölder map \(x\mapsto\sqrt{x_+}\) or endogenous retention in leaky-IV bounds.
statements.consumer: The result prevents nominal percentile claims from being reported at empirically plausible near-feasibility designs.

statements.statement: Let \(P\in\mathcal P_W\) and let \(\widetilde q\) satisfy \(\sup_{\theta\in K}|\widetilde q(\theta)-q_P(\theta)|\leq r\). The relaxed sublevel set \(\{\theta\in K:\widetilde q(\theta)\leq r\}\) has outer directed-Hausdorff loss at most \(C\sqrt r\) when \(0\leq\delta(P)\leq C_{\delta}r\), and at most \(Cr/\sqrt{\delta_0}\) when \(\delta(P)\geq\delta_0\), where \(C\) depends only on the fixed class constants.
statements.justification: This deterministic modulus is the mechanism by which one root-\(n\) score procedure adapts without regime selection.
statements.gap: Generic criterion-set rate results do not isolate the exact square-root versus linear modulus of Watson et al.'s quadratic leakage score.
statements.consumer: Any valid uniform score band immediately inherits contact and interior set-loss rates.

statements.statement: Can the contact--interior coupling handle establish, under the fixed-relevance Watson class and one observable multiplier rule, a conditional approximation strong enough that \(\widehat c_{1-\eta}\) simultaneously controls \(\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_I(P)}\sqrt n\{\widehat q_n(\theta)-q_P(\theta)\}/\widehat\sigma_n(\theta)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{ct}}(C_{\delta})\cup\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)\), while also giving a uniformly integrable \(O(n^{-1/2})\) score-band radius?
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing open step: weak convergence alone does not deliver a common conditional quantile and expected-loss bound across contact and interior laws.
statements.gap: Chernozhukov--Newey--Santos bootstrap an estimated local parameter space, while Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato couple score suprema; neither result directly supplies uniform integrability through a half-Hölder set map.
statements.consumer: Resolving the question validates one tuning-free inferential workflow for all empirically feasible slack regimes.

statements.statement: If the uniform multiplier-coupling question has an affirmative resolution, then the ridge-totalized single hull \(C_n\), defined on every sample and allowed to be empty, satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{ct}}(C_{\delta})\cup\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)}P\{\Theta_I(P)\subseteq C_n\}\geq1-\eta\). Moreover, under the stated empty-set convention for \(d_{\to}\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{ct}}(C_{\delta})}E_P[d_{\to}(C_n,\Theta_I(P))]=O(n^{-1/4})\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)}E_P[d_{\to}(C_n,\Theta_I(P))]=O(n^{-1/2})\), with the same statistic and critical-value rule.
statements.justification: The result couples honest whole-set coverage with automatic fourth-root-to-root-\(n\) geometric adaptation.
statements.gap: Romano--Shaikh deliver uniform whole-set coverage and Chernozhukov--Newey--Santos deliver constrained-model bootstrap validity, but neither gives the adaptive loss frontier for this quadratic-contact identified interval.
statements.consumer: Applied sensitivity analyses receive one confidence hull that remains valid without diagnosing whether the empirical leakage constraint is nearly binding.

statements.statement: Under the compatibility regime in the fixed-interior Gaussian-witness definition, for every \(n\) satisfying \(\bar T/\sqrt n\leq\min\{a_{\mathrm{int}}/2,(1-a_{\mathrm{int}})/2\}\) and \(2a_{\mathrm{int}}\bar T/\sqrt n+\bar T^2/n\leq1-a_{\mathrm{int}}^2-\delta_0\), uniformly over \(t\in[-\bar T,\bar T]\), the coefficient \(b_{n,t}=a_{\mathrm{int}}+t/\sqrt n\) lies in \([a_{\mathrm{int}}/2,(1+a_{\mathrm{int}})/2]\subset(0,1)\), \[(3-\sqrt5)/2\leq\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma(b_{n,t}))\leq\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma(b_{n,t}))\leq(3+\sqrt5)/2,\] \(E_{P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}}[\|W_i\|_2^8]\leq1920\{(3+\sqrt5)/2\}^4\), and \(\sigma_{P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}}(\theta)^2=4(\theta^2+b_{n,t}^2)(1+\theta^2)\in[a_{\mathrm{int}}^2,100]\) for every \(\theta\in[-2,2]\). Moreover, \(\beta=(1,0)^{\prime}\), \(\alpha=(0,b_{n,t})^{\prime}\), \(\theta_0=\check\theta=0\), \(\gamma=(0,b_{n,t})^{\prime}\), and \(\delta(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}})=1-b_{n,t}^2\geq\delta_0\). The raw endpoints are therefore defined and \(\Theta_I(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}})=[-\sqrt{1-b_{n,t}^2},\sqrt{1-b_{n,t}^2}]\subset(-1,1)\), so \(\operatorname{dist}(\Theta_I(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}),\partial K)>1\); no \(K\)-truncation occurs. Hence \(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)\) along the full compact path. The experiment \(\{P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}:t\in[-\bar T,\bar T]\}\) is locally asymptotically normal and mutually contiguous.
statements.justification: The explicit coefficient, eigenvalue, moment, score-variance, relevance, slack, and parameter-margin bounds certify that the regular LAN path belongs to the maintained fixed-interior class.
statements.gap: The contact converse needs a distinct regular comparator experiment; no published leaky-IV result states this uniform fixed-interior path membership calculation.
statements.consumer: The verified path makes the root-\(n\) lower half of the minimax frontier a claim over the maintained model rather than over an informal Gaussian analogue.

statements.statement: Fix \(\eta<1/2\), \(\bar H>0\), \(\bar T>0\), and the contact and fixed-interior Gaussian-witness compatibility regimes. There are constants \(c_{\mathrm{ct}}>0\) and \(c_{\mathrm{int}}>0\), depending only on \(\eta,\bar H,\bar T,a_{\mathrm{int}}\) and the fixed class constants, with the following properties. For every \((D_n)\in\mathfrak D_{\eta}^{\mathrm{ct}}\), there exists \(N_{\mathrm{ct}}(D)<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq N_{\mathrm{ct}}(D)\) with \(\sqrt n\geq2\bar H\), \[\sup_{h\in[0,\bar H]}E_{P_{n,h}}\!\left[d_{\to}(D_n,\Theta_I(P_{n,h}))\right]\geq c_{\mathrm{ct}}n^{-1/4}.\] For every \((D_n)\in\mathfrak D_{\eta}^{\mathrm{int}}(a_{\mathrm{int}},\bar T)\), there exists \(N_{\mathrm{int}}(D)<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq N_{\mathrm{int}}(D)\) satisfying \(\bar T/\sqrt n\leq\min\{a_{\mathrm{int}}/2,(1-a_{\mathrm{int}})/2\}\) and \(2a_{\mathrm{int}}\bar T/\sqrt n+\bar T^2/n\leq1-a_{\mathrm{int}}^2-\delta_0\), \[\sup_{t\in[-\bar T,\bar T]}E_{P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}}\!\left[d_{\to}(D_n,\Theta_I(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}))\right]\geq c_{\mathrm{int}}n^{-1/2}.\] The interior witness-membership theorem gives \(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)\) throughout this quantified regime. Together with the conditional multiplier-hull upper theorem, these inequalities give matched \(n^{-1/4}\) contact and \(n^{-1/2}\) interior frontiers under the same outer directed-loss convention.
statements.justification: The converse shows that fourth-root contact loss is information-theoretic rather than an artifact of the proposed hull.
statements.gap: It strictly sharpens Hirano--Porter's nonregularity theorem by deriving a leaky-IV directed-Hausdorff rate lower bound and matching it with an honest hull.
statements.consumer: The lower bound gives method developers a certified benchmark for comparing alternative endpoint or score procedures.

statements.statement: For each fixed \(P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)\), the raw endpoints are well defined, the maintained parameter margin gives \(\Theta_I(P)=[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]\) without \(K\)-truncation, and the endpoint map is continuously differentiable at \(\Sigma(P)\). Hence \(\sqrt n\{(\widehat\theta_-^{\mathrm{tot}},\widehat\theta_+^{\mathrm{tot}})-(\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P))\}\) has the ordinary delta-method Gaussian limit. If the uniform multiplier-coupling question has an affirmative resolution, then \(C_n\) also has root-\(n\) outer loss. This is the regular special-case reduction of Watson et al.'s smooth endpoint argument.
statements.justification: The reduction verifies that the contact-robust construction does not sacrifice the known regular behavior away from tangency.
statements.gap: Watson et al.'s argument is appropriate only after imposing a fixed positive slack; the proposition states that exact domain explicitly.
statements.consumer: Practitioners far from feasibility contact recover conventional root-\(n\) precision from the same implementation.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_W\), \(P\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n})<m_{\Sigma}/2\}=O(n^{-2})\). On the complementary event, \(\|R_n(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n})-\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq4n^{-2}/m_{\Sigma}^2\); consequently the ridge-totalized reduced forms, score, estimated influence process, and multiplier critical value differ from their inverse-defined versions by \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Thus the near-singular fallback event is asymptotically immaterial for every stated weak limit and, because confidence sets lie in compact \(K\), for the stated expected outer-loss rates.
statements.justification: The lemma makes all reported procedures measurable on singular samples while preserving their first-order contact and interior behavior.
statements.gap: Watson et al.'s implementation removes undefined rows; this result replaces that implicit conditioning by an every-sample convention and quantifies its uniform asymptotic cost.
statements.consumer: Software can return an interval or confidence hull on every dataset without altering the endpoint laws, coverage claim, or adaptive loss frontier.

sampling_model.design: Observational i.i.d. triangular arrays in the centered linear Watson leaky-instrument SEM.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \(W_i=(Z_i^{\prime},X_i,Y_i)^{\prime}\) with fixed \(d\) and uniformly bounded eighth moments.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment \(X_i\) with reduced-form relevance \(\|\beta(P)\|_2\geq c_{\beta}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; weak instruments are excluded by the fixed relevance bound.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The covariance blocks use the measurable ridge inverse \(R_n(S)=(S+n^{-2}I_d)^{-1}\) on every original and bootstrap sample. Reduced-form vectors, the regularized score derivative, and its variance are then sample plug-ins; one Gaussian multiplier process supplies the critical value without conditioning on empirical invertibility. The retained bootstrap uses exactly \(B_n\to\infty\) conditionally independent Efron \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) candidates, strict positive-slack retention, an empirical endpoint-pair law, and a Dirac fallback at the original totalized endpoint pair when no candidate is retained.

tldr: Taking Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7 quadratic sublevel-set identity as a published input, the project begins at tangent contact: raw population square-root endpoints are used only at nonnegative slack and, on the maintained contact and interior classes, the parameter margin removes the intersection with \(K\). The total positive-part plug-in endpoints have a fourth-root Gaussian law, while a fully specified \(B_n\)-draw Efron feasibility-retained bootstrap converges to a random truncated kernel and is not contact-uniform; its measurable zero-retention fallback is uniformly negligible. Every covariance-based sample object is totalized by one measurable \(n^{-2}\) ridge rule. Conditional on resolving the stated uniform multiplier coupling, inversion before the square-root map gives whole-set coverage, \(n^{-1/4}\) contact loss, and \(n^{-1/2}\) fixed-interior loss under one rule, with both rates matched by explicit contact and interior Gaussian LAN paths.

project_justification.gap: Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7 provide the \(p=2\) sharp quadratic sublevel-set identity and its raw endpoint representation at nonnegative slack, and their Theorem 4 supplies a feasibility-retained bootstrap workflow. They do not derive the fourth-root contact law, the random retained-resample kernel for the fully specified finite Monte Carlo algorithm, contact-uniform validity, a whole-identified-set score hull, or a minimax loss frontier. Existing boundary and directional-bootstrap theory does not supply those leaky-IV results.
project_justification.niche: The published scalar quadratic score remains regular at tangent contact even though the endpoint square root is only half-Hölder. Calibrating the score before endpoint transformation creates a route to uniform set inference and makes both contact and interior local minimax geometry explicit.
project_justification.fill: The project keeps the identified set as an always-defined \(K\)-restricted sublevel set, proves when its partial raw endpoints are untruncated, derives the fourth-root contact law and the retained random kernel for an exact Efron algorithm with a negligible measurable fallback, proves nonuniformity for the named workflow, constructs an every-sample multiplier score hull using a common ridge convention, and, conditional on the uniform multiplier coupling, matches its adaptive contact and interior loss rates with certified Gaussian LAN converses.

technical_internal_limitation: The early kill test is confined to the Gaussian witness under the stated compatibility regime \(C_{\delta}\geq\bar H\) and the explicit covariance, moment, score-variance, relevance, and \(K\)-interiority bounds. Failure of uniform integrability for the score-band radius would preserve coverage but invalidate the expected-loss claims.
honest_scope: Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7 quadratic sharp-set reduction is a published input: the identified set is always the \(K\)-restricted score sublevel set, whereas its raw square-root endpoints are partial analytic objects defined only at nonnegative slack. The maintained parameter margin removes \(K\)-truncation on the contact-local and fixed-interior classes where endpoint limits are stated. The contribution begins with the exact contact endpoint law, the random retained kernel for the specified \(B_n\)-candidate Efron algorithm, and named-workflow nonuniformity; the algorithm's zero-retention fallback is measurable and uniformly negligible on the witness. The genuinely open content is one observable multiplier approximation strong enough for uniform whole-set coverage and expected adaptive loss over contact-local and fixed-interior laws. The upper hull and its rates are conditional on an affirmative resolution of that question. All finite-sample covariance operations use the stated ridge convention, the directed loss is defined when a random hull is empty, and both Gaussian lower-bound paths have explicit maintained-class membership regimes. The model keeps \(d\) fixed, assumes a known scalar leakage radius, and excludes weak instruments.
novelty_justification: The exact \(p=2\) score reduction and the \(K\)-intersected raw endpoint representation on its proper nonnegative-slack domain are credited entirely to Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7. The novelty kernel starts with the fourth-root positive-part Gaussian endpoint law and the random truncated kernel generated by the fully specified finite Monte Carlo version of the feasibility-retained workflow in their Theorem 4, followed by a direct contact-nonuniformity result for that workflow. The constructive advance is one totalized quadratic-score hull with conditional uniform whole-set coverage and automatically changing expected outer-loss rates, matched by fully quantified contact and interior Gaussian LAN lower bounds. Li's proximal bootstrap does not subsume this kernel because it treats root-\(n\) constrained point estimators rather than partially identified sets.
